finding: ProjectData.assets is a dead field: exportProject() hardcodes assets:[] and nothing in the codebase ever reads data.assets, so the media library is NOT part of the project snapshot and survives only via IndexedDB plus the server.
evidence: Composer.ts:608 'assets: [],'; grep for '.assets' in Composer.ts returns only that line; AssetData is referenced solely by its own declarations (shared/types/asset.ts:13, shared/types/index.ts:189) and shared/types/project.ts:40 'assets: AssetData[];' — zero readers, zero writers. Persistence is IndexedDB db 'aquibra-media' v1 (IndexedDBAdapter.ts:14-21, stores assets/folders/blobs) + Prisma media_assets (schema.prisma:1015).
fix: Either delete ProjectData.assets and AssetData (dead type, per the no-dead-code rule), or make exportProject emit the asset manifest so a project export/import/version-restore carries its library. Today a project JSON export loses every asset reference silently.
chain: Media -> MediaAsset -> exportProject -> (nothing) -> Project snapshot -> library absent from every project export, version and restore

finding: A placed image references its asset by raw URL STRING, never by asset id, so the element and the library have no durable link — every usage lookup is a string scan and any URL change silently orphans the element.
evidence: useMediaState.ts:256 'composer.mediaOps.insertMediaAt(asset.src, mediaType, { path: "click" })' passes asset.src; ElementManager.ts:466 'attributes: { src },' — the element stores only the URL. The reverse lookup is ElementManager.ts:530-548 findByMediaSrc, a string compare over this.elements.values() plus a background-image substring test. Prisma has no reverse reference either: MediaAsset has no relation to Page, and Page.blocks is opaque Json (schema.prisma:577-599).
fix: Store the asset id on the element (data-asset-id) alongside src, and resolve src from it at render/export. Everything downstream — delete safety, version restore, blob-URL repair, publish checks — currently reimplements string matching because the identity edge does not exist.

finding: The reload repair for dead blob: URLs only fixes the src ATTRIBUTE — a background-image set from a local asset is never repaired and stays broken forever.
evidence: MediaManager.ts:768-790 loadFromStorage rebuilds object URLs and emits LOCAL_URLS_REBUILT with a remapped old->new map; Composer.ts:391-398 repairLocalMediaUrls reads only 'element.getAttributes().src' and calls 'element.setAttribute("src", next)'. No background-image branch — unlike MediaCommandLayer.setElementSrc (MediaCommandLayer.ts:437-455) and deleteWithGrace (:98-102), which both handle url() backgrounds. BackgroundSection.tsx:248 writes exactly that shape: onChange("background-image", `url('${asset.src}')`).
fix: Give repairLocalMediaUrls the same two-branch read/write MediaCommandLayer already has, and reuse one helper rather than a third copy of the src/background-image pair.

finding: Deleting an asset hard-deletes the Vercel Blob with no page reference check anywhere, and because publish hot-links that blob URL, the delete breaks the LIVE published site with no warning and no way to detect it.
evidence: server/services/media.service.ts:320 deletes the row first, then :337-340 counts only 'other MediaAsset/MediaAssetVersion rows sharing this url' and :341-343 'if (otherAssetRefs === 0 && otherVersionRefs === 0) { await del(asset.url); }' — no page/element check exists. lib/publish-files.ts:53-68 maps p.html through five string injectors and never touches src attributes, so the deployment ships the blob URL verbatim; the worker uploads pages + robots.txt + sitemap.xml only (:76,:83). The editor's own guard, MediaCommandLayer.deleteWithGrace (:88-133), clears element srcs in THIS session's document only and cannot reach the deployed HTML — which PublishBuildJob.log retains verbatim (publish.service.ts:340), so even a rollback restores markup pointing at a deleted blob.
fix: Before del(), refuse or warn when the URL appears in any live page's blocks JSON for the workspace; and make the editor's delete confirm say 'used on N pages, M of them published' rather than only counting in-session elements.
chain: Media -> MediaAsset -> deleteAsset -> del(blob) -> Publish/Pages -> every published 404s, on a site nobody edited

finding: Alt text is captured, AI-generated, stored and synced — and never reaches the page. No code path copies MediaAsset.altText onto a placed element, so every published image ships with no alt attribute.
evidence: The asset side is complete: useAltTextAutoTrigger.ts:64-71 writes altText after upload, AssetUploadService.ts:193-200 mirrors it to the server, media_assets.altText exists (schema.prisma:1024). The element side is empty: ElementManager.ts:466 creates the element with 'attributes: { src },' and nothing else. Repo-wide grep for setAttribute("alt" in src/engine + src/editor returns exactly two hits, both CMS binding — DataBindResolver.ts:102 (binds data["name"]) and useCMSPreview.ts:77. The Inspector has zero references to altText.
fix: Set alt from asset.altText in insertMediaAt (and in replaceMedia), and add an Alt text field to the Inspector's image section so a user can fix it on the element. Until then the AI alt-text feature has no output surface at all.
chain: Media -> MediaAsset.altText -> insertMediaAt -> (nothing) -> Canvas/Export/Publish -> every published has no alt; SEO and a11y both blind

finding: Pre-publish checks never look at image sources, so a site whose pages carry device-only blob: URLs is reported 'ready to publish'.
evidence: server/services/publish.service.ts:18-108 runPrePublishChecks builds exactly six checks — Vercel connected (:59), Pages ready (:69), SEO configured (:75), Domain connected (:82), Empty pages (:89), Favicon (:101) — and 'ready' is just !hasFail (:107). No check reads page blocks for unresolvable src. The editor knows the fact at insert time (useMediaState.ts:264-273 warns 'it won't show on the page or publish') and throws it away; nothing carries it to the publish gate.
fix: Add a 'Media resolvable' check that scans live pages' blocks for blob:/data: srcs and any URL not on the blob host, returning warning (or fail) with a count. The editor already has the localOnly count in LibraryManager.tsx:170-171 to seed it.
chain: Media -> localOnly asset -> Publish -> runPrePublishChecks -> Publish tab -> 'ready' shown over a site that will ship broken images

finding: AI alt-text provenance is device-local: generatedMetadata is written to IndexedDB, read by the panel badge, never synced, and never rebuilt from the server — even though the Prisma column exists.
evidence: Written locally at useAltTextAutoTrigger.ts:65-71 ('generatedMetadata: { altText: { generatedAt, model } }'); read at mediaUtils.ts:75 'generatedAltMeta: asset.generatedMetadata?.altText,' and AssetDetailsPanel.tsx:385. But AssetUploadService.ts:193-200 sends only filename and altText, and MediaManager.importServerAssets (:490-522) constructs the asset without generatedMetadata. media_assets.generatedMetadata exists (schema.prisma:1026) and the router never reads or writes it.
fix: Include generatedMetadata in remoteSync.updateAsset and in importServerAssets, or drop the badge — right now the same asset shows 'AI-generated by X' on the machine that uploaded it and nothing anywhere else.

finding: Media does not use the composer event bus at all: it runs a private emitter, so the ASSET_* family on the composer bus is dead and nothing outside media can subscribe to a media change through the normal channel.
evidence: ASSET_UPLOADED / ASSET_DELETED / ASSET_SELECTED are declared at shared/constants/events.ts:377-379 and named nowhere else in src/ (confirmed by repo-wide grep). MediaManager extends MediaEventEmitter (MediaManager.ts:120), whose listeners live in its own Map (MediaEventEmitter.ts:14) with a protected emit (:38) — reachable only via composer.media.on(). MEDIA_EVENTS (shared/constants/media.ts:83-149) is a parallel 22-name namespace. Exactly ONE media event crosses to the composer bus: Composer.ts:412 subscribes to MEDIA_EVENTS.LOCAL_URLS_REBUILT.
fix: Either delete the three ASSET_* constants (dead code) or bridge the media emitter onto the composer bus so cross-module listeners have one place to subscribe. Today any module wanting a media signal must reach into composer.media directly, which is why only 3 files outside the media tree do.

finding: Seven media events are emitted with zero listeners, and an eighth is declared but never emitted — the whole insert/replace telemetry surface is write-only.
evidence: Measured by grepping on(MEDIA_EVENTS.X) across src/ excluding tests: INSERT_SUCCEEDED=0, INSERT_FAILED=0, REPLACE_OPENED=0, REPLACE_COMMITTED=0, REPLACE_PARTIAL=0, REPLACE_ROLLED_BACK=0, UPLOAD_START=0 listeners. All six replace/insert events are emitted from MediaCommandLayer.ts (:167,:174,:196,:230,:262,:272,:281). LIBRARY_OPENED (constants/media.ts:148) is never emitted OR listened to — its only appearance outside the constant is MediaErrors.test.ts:90, a test that asserts the string's value and therefore proves nothing about the product.
fix: REPLACE_PARTIAL is the one that costs a user something: replaceAcross commits partial batches and emits the failed list (MediaCommandLayer.ts:262-267) but the comment at :270 says 'the UI should display' it and no UI subscribes — the caller only reads result.clean. Wire REPLACE_PARTIAL to a dialog, wire INSERT_FAILED to the toast the panel currently duplicates by hand, and delete LIBRARY_OPENED.
chain: Media -> replaceAcross partial failure -> REPLACE_PARTIAL -> (no listener) -> Canvas/Toast -> user is told the replace succeeded while N elements still show the old image

finding: QUOTA_EXCEEDED has no listener and the code comments claim it does; the typed quota error degrades into a generic 'upload failed' toast, so a user who fills their storage is never told that is why.
evidence: MediaManager.ts:848-849 comment: 'Emits QUOTA_EXCEEDED (the library banner subscribes)'. It does not — on(MEDIA_EVENTS.QUOTA_EXCEEDED) has 0 hits in src/; StorageQuotaBar.tsx:45 is a pure props component (used, total, onOptimize). The typed MediaQuotaError carrying rescueAction 'show-quota-banner' (MediaStorageTypes.ts:57-72) is thrown at MediaManager.ts:859, lands as a rejection inside Promise.allSettled (useUploadState.ts:190-196), and surfaces as useUploadState.ts:207-209 'N uploads failed'. Only the click-insert path maps the error name to a real message (useMediaState.ts:288).
fix: Subscribe the quota banner to QUOTA_EXCEEDED, or have useUploadState inspect the rejection's rescueAction instead of counting failures. Correct the MediaManager comment either way — it is the reason nobody noticed.
chain: Media -> storage quota -> QUOTA_EXCEEDED -> (no listener) -> StorageQuotaBar -> the banner that exists to explain the failure never opens

finding: Renaming a folder does not refresh the folder tree: FOLDER_UPDATED is emitted and has zero listeners, while its two siblings FOLDER_CREATED and FOLDER_DELETED are both subscribed.
evidence: MediaManager.renameFolder emits at :1471 'this.emit(MEDIA_EVENTS.FOLDER_UPDATED, updated);'. useLibraryState.ts subscribes reloadFolders to FOLDER_CREATED and FOLDER_DELETED only (both present in the grep, FOLDER_UPDATED absent). Measured listener counts: FOLDER_CREATED=1, FOLDER_DELETED=1, FOLDER_UPDATED=0.
fix: Add FOLDER_UPDATED to the same subscription list in useLibraryState — a one-line fix for a rename that appears not to have worked.
chain: Media -> MediaFolder -> renameFolder -> FOLDER_UPDATED -> (no listener) -> folder rail -> the old name stays on screen until the panel remounts

finding: Two delete doors with different contracts, and one component holds both: the raw path deletes with no undo and leaves every referencing element with a dead src.
evidence: Safe path: MediaCommandLayer.deleteWithGrace (:88-133) trashes the asset, clears src and background-image on every element from findByMediaSrc (:97-103), and offers one undo that restores both — called at MediaLibraryPanel.tsx:130 and useSelectionState.ts:177. Raw path: useMediaManager.ts:81 'await composer.media.deleteAsset(assetId);' → MediaManager.deleteAsset (:1069-1074) → finalizeDelete (:1125-1157), which touches storage, the object URL, the retry queues and the server row and never looks at an element. MediaLibraryPanel.tsx imports useMediaManager at :14 and destructures it at :67 while also calling deleteWithGrace at :130 — both doors are live in the same file.
fix: Delete the deleteAsset passthrough from useMediaManager (its only consumer is MediaLibraryPanel, which already uses the safe path) and make MediaManager.deleteAsset engine-internal, so deleteWithGrace is the only public delete.

finding: Audio is permanently device-only AND invisible to every local-only warning, because the flag those warnings read is never set for it.
evidence: toServerAssetType returns null for audio (MediaManager.ts:60-61), so the entire server-mirror block 'if (this.remoteSync && serverType)' (MediaManager.ts:962) is skipped and asset.localOnly is never assigned — MediaManager.ts:1043-1044 states the intent: 'serverType=null (audio) means we keep the asset local without queuing'. Every warning keys on that flag: the upload toast (useUploadState.ts:128), the insert warning (useMediaState.ts:264), the replace warning (:232), the canvas-drop warning (useDropExecution.ts:261), the 'N not on the server' pill (LibraryManager.tsx:449-452). Meanwhile ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES.AUDIO admits five audio types (constants/media.ts:49) that the upload route's allowlist does not carry (asset-upload/route.ts:31-50). Distinct from W-A-18, which files the drop-zone/server mismatch; this is the warning system being blind to it.
fix: Set localOnly = true for audio at upload (it is, definitionally, local only) so the existing four warnings and the sync pill cover it — or drop audio from ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES until the server has a schema for it.

finding: The font-upload guidance toast can never fire — it reads a field the event payload does not have — so the one asset type that cannot be placed on the canvas never tells the user where it went.
evidence: useUploadState.ts:126 'if (p?.mimeType?.includes("font"))' but the UPLOAD_COMPLETE payload is emitted at MediaManager.ts:1051-1055 as '{ success: true, asset: finalAsset, fileName: file.name }' — mimeType exists only at p.asset.mimeType. The branch is dead, so the fallback 'File uploaded ✓' fires for fonts. Fonts genuinely cannot be inserted: insertMediaAt routes type 'font' to a font-family application on selected text and fails with 'no-text-selected' otherwise (ElementManager.ts:395-421); the only place the instruction survives is a click on an already-uploaded font (useMediaState.ts:218).
fix: Read p.asset.mimeType (or add mimeType to the emit). One-character-class fix on a toast that has been unreachable since the payload shape changed.

finding: Inserting an icon produces an element that cannot render: the icon NAME is passed as the src and the icon type serializes to a bare <span>.
evidence: Three call sites pass icon.name as src — MediaTab.tsx:218 'composer.mediaOps.insertMedia(icon.name, "icon")', MediaTab.tsx:401 (IconBrowserOverlay onPick), LibraryManager.tsx:206 — each followed by a success toast ('${icon.name} icon added ✓'). insertMediaAt maps icon -> element type 'icon' (ElementManager.ts:429) and creates it with attributes:{src} (:466); TYPE_TO_TAG_MAP maps icon -> 'span' (shared/utils/html/typeMapping.ts:159), so the document gets <span src="User"> and shows nothing. Grep for icon-specific rendering in src/engine returns only MediaManager.ts:59. 'lottie' is a valid MediaInsertType (MediaCommandLayer.ts:36) and is absent from TYPE_TO_TAG_MAP entirely, so it falls through to div with the same result. Note DiscIcon already carries a usable svgDataUrl (MediaManager.ts:93) that these call sites ignore.
fix: Pass the icon's svgDataUrl (or render the icon element from its name in the serializer). Until then every icon inserted from the picker is an invisible span over a green toast.

finding: The engine's file-size ceiling is up to ten times the server's, so a file that validates locally is refused server-side and silently becomes a device-only asset.
evidence: Engine: MEDIA_SIZE_LIMITS.MAX_VIDEO_SIZE = 100MB, MAX_AUDIO_SIZE = 50MB, MAX_IMAGE_SIZE = 10MB (shared/constants/media.ts:18-22), enforced by validateFile (MediaHelpers.ts:18-28). Server: MAX_FILE_BYTES = 50MB (asset-upload/route.ts:52) clamped by plan — 'const planMaxMB = PLAN_LIMITS[quota.tier].fileUploadMaxMB' / 'Math.min(MAX_FILE_BYTES, planMaxMB * 1024 * 1024)' (:116-117), with FREE at 10MB (lib/constants/plan-limits.ts:36). A 30MB video on FREE passes validateFile, fails the token mint, and uploadAndCreate returns null (AssetUploadService.ts:136-139), which MediaManager reads as offline and marks localOnly + queues retry (MediaManager.ts:1039-1041) — a retry that will fail forever. Separate from W-A-20, which is about the board's stated limit.
fix: Derive the engine limit from the plan (the panel already fetches it via useServerStorageQuota) so the failure is a named validation error at pick time, and do not queue a retry for a size rejection.

finding: ZIP export drops device-only assets and never consults the media library at all — it regex-scrapes its own HTML and matches on file extension, which a blob: URL does not have.
evidence: AssetBundler.isImageUrl (engine/export/AssetBundler.ts:123-126): 'const imageExts = [".png",".jpg",".jpeg",".gif",".webp",".svg",".ico"]; return imageExts.some((ext) => lowerUrl.includes(ext));' — a blob:http://host/<uuid> src matches none, so it is neither fetched (:153) nor rewritten (:198), and the ZIP ships a dead src. The blurb promises otherwise: ExportModal.tsx:190 'A .zip with every page, one stylesheet and your media — host it anywhere.' Export also has no link to the module: nothing under engine/export or editor/export imports engine/media or reads composer.media; discovery is entirely regex (AssetBundler.ts:73,:85,:105).
fix: Resolve the export's asset list from MediaManager (which holds the Blob for every local asset) instead of scraping URLs, so a local-only asset exports as real bytes rather than a dead reference.

finding: Brand/Settings favicon and og-image never touch the media library — all three fields are raw URL text inputs, while the Inspector's src field right next door has a Browse button.
evidence: Editor favicon: SiteSettingsScreen.tsx:123-129 '<Field label="Favicon URL"><Input type="text" value={favicon} placeholder="https://example.com/favicon.ico" />' — no upload, no picker. Site OG image: SeoScreen.tsx:111-122 (type="url", validated only by /^https?:\/\/\S+$/i at :41). Per-page OG image: SocialTab.tsx:69-76. The picker exists and is wired everywhere else: PropertyField.tsx:159-166 renders a Browse button that calls onOpenMediaLibrary([mediaType], asset => onChange("src", asset.src)), and BackgroundSection.tsx:78 and :247 do the same for background-image; the chain runs AquibraStudio.tsx:580 -> StudioPanels.tsx:510 -> ProInspector.tsx:559 -> InspectorTabContent.tsx:204 -> useContentModals.ts:89-95 -> StudioModals.tsx:172. The dashboard's own favicon upload is a third, disjoint pipeline (settings-tab.tsx:75-76 trpc.upload.presign/confirm -> app/api/upload/[fileId]/route.ts:91) that never creates a MediaAsset row.
fix: Pass onOpenMediaLibrary into the settings/SEO screens and add the same Browse button. A user who has just uploaded their logo cannot select it as a favicon; they must copy a blob-storage URL by hand.
chain: Brand/Settings -> favicon + ogImage -> set value -> (no media library edge) -> Media -> user retypes a URL for a file already in their library

finding: CMS image fields are declared end to end and reach the media library nowhere — the record form has no image branch and falls through to a plain text box (control gap already filed as W-C-15; the module edge is the new part).
evidence: Type exists: shared/types/cms.ts:17 '| "image"'; offered in the builder ContentViews.tsx:441 and CMSCollectionSetupModal.tsx:178; ecommerce seeds one (shared/types/ecommerce.ts:106-107). The table view even knows about it — CMSRecordsModal.tsx:377 renders a MediaCell — but that cell only reports presence (:59-65 '✓ {label}' / '— missing'). renderField (CMSRecordsModal.tsx:192-241) branches on boolean, textarea/richtext and select only, then :236 'const inputType = field.type === "number" ? "number" : ... : "text";' and :240-241 renders a TextInput. The sidebar record form has the same shape (ContentViews.tsx:351). Neither imports anything from the media tree.
fix: Give renderField an image branch that calls onOpenMediaLibrary — the same prop the Inspector already threads down — and render a thumbnail. See W-C-15 for the full field-coverage gap.
chain: Content -> CMS image field -> renderField -> (no media library edge) -> Media -> a collection whose whole point is images is filled by pasting URLs

finding: Restoring an asset version repoints the library at a new URL and leaves every placed element on the old one — in an overlay that has already computed the element list.
evidence: AssetDetailOverlay.confirmRestore (:140-155) calls restoreAssetVersion(versionId).then(res => onUpdate?.(item.key, { src: res.url })) — it updates the library item and nothing else. Server-side the parent asset's url and bytes are rewritten (server/services/media.service.ts:477-480). The same component computes usage by page eleven lines later (:158-166 collectUsageByPage) and offers a jump-to-element handler (:169-175), so the element list is right there. The sibling surface does it correctly: AssetDetailsPanel.tsx:234 calls composer.mediaOps.replaceAcross(versions[0].src, v.src).
fix: Call replaceAcross(item.src, res.url) inside confirmRestore, matching AssetDetailsPanel. Also note restoreAssetVersion does not snapshot the outgoing URL as a new version (media.service.ts:457-481), so restore is one-way unless the caller saved one first.

finding: MediaAsset has no foreign key to Site or User, so deleting a site (or a user account) leaves every asset row and every paid blob behind, and no job reclaims them.
evidence: prisma/schema.prisma:1015-1040 — 'userId String' and 'siteId String?' are bare columns; the only @relation declarations are versions (:1032) and folder (:1033). Page cascades on site delete (:594 'onDelete: Cascade') but media does not. app/api/cron/soft-delete-purge deletes sites with a single site.deleteMany and touches no media; account-deletion/route.ts:60 deletes the user and leaves media_assets. Repo-wide, del() is imported in exactly one file (media.service.ts:2) and no cron route mentions blob or mediaAsset. Three separate comments defer to a reconciliation job that does not exist (media.service.ts:329,:346; asset-upload/route.ts:238-239).
fix: Add the FK + cascade, or add the reconciliation cron the comments promise. There are at least five orphan-blob sources today, including plan-cap version pruning (media.service.ts:446) which never calls del().

finding: BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN is required by BOTH upload routes (not just cleanup), the two fail with different status codes, and neither says 'storage is not configured' — so a misconfigured deploy looks exactly like the user being offline.
evidence: Media library: app/api/asset-upload/route.ts mints the client token via handleUpload (:21), and a missing token throws into the catch at :257 whose mapping (:260-263) matches neither 'Unauthenticated' nor 'quota'/'limit', returning 400. Favicon/og-image: app/api/upload/[fileId]/route.ts:70 calls put() directly and returns 500 'Blob upload failed' (:78-81). The editor cannot tell either apart from a network failure — AssetUploadService.ts:136-139 catches everything and returns null, and MediaManager reads null as offline, setting localOnly and queueing a retry that will never succeed (MediaManager.ts:1039-1041).
fix: Return a distinguishable configuration error from both routes and surface it as 'media storage isn't configured' rather than the offline copy. Confirms the root CLAUDE.md note that this var is load-bearing for uploads, not only cleanup.

finding: The two media UI trees import into each other, so neither is the owner and there is no single door to the library.
evidence: editor/media/LibraryManager.tsx pulls eight modules out of the panel tree (:17 useMediaState, :18 StockSourceModal, :19 ConfirmDeleteModal, :20 MediaContextMenu, :23 AssetDetailOverlay, :27 LibraryItem, :32 FolderBreadcrumb, :34 formatQuotaSize) while sidebar/tabs/media/components/AssetDetailOverlay.tsx:28 imports back the other way ('@/editor/media/OptimizationPanel'). Two separate library surfaces then mount from these trees — MediaLibraryPanel (StudioModals.tsx:172, the Inspector's picker) and LibraryManager (FullPageRouter.tsx:15-16) — with different delete paths (see MOD-E-12) and different version UIs (see MOD-E-20).
fix: Pick one owner directory and one library component; the divergences filed in MOD-E-12 and MOD-E-20 are both consequences of maintaining two.

finding: Media is scoped to a site by a soft filter that deliberately lets unscoped rows through, so pre-scoping assets stay visible in every site in the same browser.
evidence: MediaManager.loadFromStorage:750-753 — 'this.projectId ? rows.filter(r => r.siteId === this.projectId || r.siteId == null) : rows' with the comment at :747-749 explaining that siteId == null survives on purpose because those rows may be local-only. setProjectId (:441-452) re-reads and emits INITIALIZED. The IndexedDB store carries no site index (IndexedDBAdapter.ts:66-71 indexes type/folderId/createdAt/tags only), so the filter is a post-read scan.
fix: Nothing to change today — the tradeoff is documented and deliberate. Worth a one-time migration that stamps legacy rows with their owning site so the exception can be closed, since it is the last path by which one site can list another's files.
